intro: Lesson 10: Design and make a page: rivers or the Romans. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

bullets: Rivers begin at a source, often a spring in the hills, and end at a mouth, usually the sea.
The River Thames is about 346 km long and flows through London to the North Sea.
A meander is a bend in a river.
The water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.
The Romans built Londinium beside the Thames, where they could cross the river.

questions.q: Write three facts for the page from the project notes.
questions.a: For example: rivers begin at a source; the Romans built roads; Londinium was a Roman town.

questions.q: Make your page in the DTP tool using your plan; save the draft to the portal.
questions.a: A complete draft meeting the checklist.

questions.q: Extend: add a 'Did you know?' box.

questions.a: A) who the page is for. Design for your reader.

questions.q: Think again: Would a page for Year 1 look the same as a page for grown-ups? Why not?
questions.a: No: bigger text, simpler words and bright pictures for younger readers.
